scope: US-first, globally extensible research coverage; no entity-specific accounting conclusions
interpretation: Question families and subsector prompts are original editorial screening proposals. They do not establish applicability, missing coverage, or correct accounting treatment. Candidate corpus records are navigation seeds, not validated coverage claims.

initial_research_waves.focus: Map the existing corpus and complete shared accounting foundations
initial_research_waves.why: Reuse existing general material; inspect payroll, benefits, management costing, capital instruments and entity events instead of mistaking sparse tags for missing sources.

initial_research_waves.focus: Manufacturing, retail/wholesale, software and professional services
initial_research_waves.why: Contrast inventory conversion, distribution, subscriptions and labor-based projects with the construction model.

initial_research_waves.focus: Property, transport, hospitality, agriculture and extraction
initial_research_waves.why: Expose asset ownership, lease roles, perishability, resource stages and fleet or site obligations.

initial_research_waves.focus: Financial institutions, healthcare, education, nonprofit and government
initial_research_waves.why: Separate reporting frameworks, regulatory populations, funds and payer arrangements. Existing specialist sources provide starting points.

initial_research_waves.focus: Every remaining subsector, detailed-industry exceptions and additional jurisdictions
initial_research_waves.why: Close the finite inventory systematically, review heterogeneous residual categories, and extend through versioned international crosswalks.
